sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 46.6% a year from $6.91 billion in FY2017 to $215.9 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F211].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 6.8% in FY2020 and was flat in FY2023, then grew 125.9% in FY2024, 114.2% in FY2025 and 65.5% in FY2026 [D130][D284][D338][D393][D448].
The FY2024 step change came from Data Center revenue up 217% on Hopper GPU shipments for generative AI [P23][P25].
FY2026 growth was again data center compute and networking, with Blackwell the majority of Data Center revenue [P10].
Data Center was 89.7% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 60.2pp of the 65.5% growth [D620][D622][D448].
Data Center computing grew 59% on Blackwell demand and networking grew 142% on NVLink and Ethernet ramps [P8].
Networking contributed 14.1pp of FY2026 growth, up from 7.2pp in FY2025 [D636][D633].
Operating income grew 60.1% against revenue growth of 65.5%, an incremental margin of 57.3% [D449][D448][D475].
Diluted EPS grew 66.7% in FY2026, slightly ahead of net income growth of 64.7%, as the diluted share count fell 1.2% [D452][D450][D470].
Operating margin was 60.4% in FY2026, below the FY2025 window high of 62.4% but far above the 32.8% window median [F50][D812][D813].
Gross margin fell 3.9pp to 71.1%, the main drag on the operating margin, which slipped 2.0pp [D462][F30][D463].
Compute & Networking operating income absorbed a $4.5 billion H20 excess inventory and purchase obligation charge in the first quarter [P7].
Operating expenses rose 40.7%, driven by compensation, employee growth and compute and infrastructure costs [D468][P9].
Net margin of 55.6% trailed operating margin by 4.8pp, as other income of $11.1 billion partly offset a 15.1% tax rate [F70][F50][D861][X120][D434].
Operating cash flow of $102.7 billion was 0.86x net income, the window low and below the 0.97x median [F100][D435][D850][D851].
Free cash flow was $96.7 billion, a 44.8% margin, after capex of $6.04 billion [F110][D432][F105].
Capex ran at 2.13x D&A and 2.8% of revenue, up from 1.74x and 2.5% in FY2025 [D437][D431][D382][D376].
Inventory grew 112.3% and receivables 66.8%, both faster than revenue, holding conversion below net income [D474][D473][D448].
Cash and equivalents were $10.6 billion against total debt of $8.47 billion in FY2026 [F150][D440].
The pack omits FY2026 short-term investments, so net cash and its peer rank cannot be read across the gap [R3].
Buybacks of $40.1 billion plus dividends of $974 million equal 42.5% of free cash flow [X150][X160][D444].
Return on average equity was 101.5%, in the 100th percentile of six semis peers against a 20.3% median [D447][D848][D849].
Short-term investments were not reported in FY2026 after $34.6 billion in FY2025, so net cash and its peer rank are understated [R3][X188].
Two direct customers represented 22% and 14% of FY2026 revenue, all primarily in Compute & Networking [P6].
China revenue fell 21.4% in FY2026, a 4.1pp drag, after contributing 20.9pp in FY2025 [D545][D546][D543].
The $4.5 billion H20 charge shows product-transition and export risk can hit gross margin within a single quarter [P7].
If gross margin holds above the FY2025 high of 75.0%, the FY2026 3.9pp decline was a one-off charge; a further fall below 71.1% would confirm mix or provision pressure [D818][D462][F30].
Operating cash flow at or above 0.97x net income would restore the window median conversion; a second year below 0.86x would point to working capital strain [D851][D435].
China revenue recovering above the FY2025 level of $25.0 billion would reverse the FY2026 decline; a further drop would extend the 4.1pp drag [S23][D546].
